articles.title: Volunteers Turn Out for the Winter Cleanup Across Stonebridge
articles.deck: Residents of Stonebridge filled the hall on Sunday to ask questions about the plan.
body: Lamar Underhill, who has lived in Stonebridge for 9 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. The Stonebridge Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
The plan calls for basketball court along Ingram Street, with work expected to start in January. Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Sunday mornings.

articles.title: Parish and Park Groups Team Up on Community Oven
articles.deck: Residents of Foundry Row filled the hall on Friday to ask questions about the plan.
body: The plan calls for community oven along Laurel Drive, with work expected to start in September. Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Friday mornings.
Nora Wojcik, who has lived in Foundry Row for 21 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
Public works estimates the work will take about 21 weeks once it begins.

articles.title: Cedar Hollow Primary Parents Organize Summer Concert Series
articles.deck: The program begins in August and is open to all students in grade 6 and up.
body: Principal Denise Corrigan said the program was built with help from parents and local volunteers.
Students will meet on Tuesday afternoons in the Millrace library, and transportation will be provided for those who need it. The board will review the results at the end of the winter term.
Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for August.

body: Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Saturday mornings. Andre Fairbanks, who has lived on Ridge Lane for 26 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
The Tannery Flats Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.

articles.title: Eastgate Asks Council for Speed Limit Change
articles.deck: The vote came after 37 residents spoke at Sunday’s session.
body: Public works estimates the work will take about 37 weeks once it starts in November.
Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

articles.title: Nelson Chandler, 80, Machinist
articles.deck: Friends remember Nelson Chandler for the many years of service to Tannery Flats.
body: Born in Tannery Flats in the years after the war, Nelson Chandler spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood. Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Canal Park Food Pantry in his or her name.
Nelson Chandler died in March at home on Orion Lane, at the age of 80. Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Tannery Flats.

articles.title: Millrace Middle School Adds Second Recycling Drop-off to Spring Schedule
articles.deck: Principal Margaret Hartigan said the school is grateful to families who volunteered this year.
body: Students will meet on Monday afternoons in the Kettle Hill Park gate, and transportation will be provided for those who need it.
Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for March.
The board will review the results at the end of the spring term.

articles.title: Letter: Support the Park Bench Program
body: To the editor: I have lived on Pine Avenue for 18 years, and I want to say what a difference the Stonebridge Trail Crew has made. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.
I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the June meeting.
Hannah Zielinski, Foxglove Heights

articles.title: Letter: St. Brendan’s Parish Did a Good Job This Spring
body: To the editor: Please keep the basketball court in the budget. Many of us on Mulberry Avenue use it every week.
To the editor: I have lived on Mulberry Avenue for 4 years, and I want to say what a difference St. Brendan’s Parish has made.
Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed. I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the July meeting.
Lorraine Underhill, Bellwood

articles.title: The Stonebridge Trail Crew Hosts Second Recycling Drop-off on Friday
articles.deck: Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public.
body: Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public. Organizers ask guests to bring a dish to share or a little cash for supplies.

articles.title: The Upper Commons Historical Society Plans Playground Upgrade for Winter
articles.deck: The work is expected to take 37 weeks and will be paid for with $25,000 raised locally.
body: The group has raised $25,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Mill Hill town hall on Wednesday at 7 p.m.
The effort began in April when a handful of neighbors met at the Mill Hill town hall to talk about playground upgrade.
Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Wednesday mornings.
